column2: The Sicilian uprising has been scheduled
The Sicilian Districts Report to Naples

The island offices submit their returns amid the constitutional agitation. Paid works, provincial accounts and the conduct of the magistrates have given Palermo reasons to judge the government by more than its promises. The ministers must keep the offices supplied and respect the local arrangements on which their cooperation depends. An unfulfilled programme or renewed disorder could still undo that confidence.
Maintain the works and hear the island deputations.
Sicilian administrative confidence has been reported

Men hesitate to fire upon volunteers fighting under the Italian tricolour. Desertions thin the ranks, officers dispute their orders, and the royal army struggles to rally shaken formations for another battle.

Reports from Sicily speak of soldiers deserting their posts and officers unable to rally their men. The volunteers advance beneath the Italian tricolour, and many in the royal ranks shrink from firing upon them. Loyal regiments still hold their positions, but contradictory orders and doubts about the crown have shaken the army. The ministers can command another battle. They cannot be certain who will fight it.
Restore confidence and coordinate the remaining commands.
The royal army has faced the historical invasion crisis
The political or military circumstances behind the royal army's crisis have changed. The commands must now organise their obligations under the present government.
Close the emergency and revise the command accounts.
